conceptual_explanation: Inversion means putting the auxiliary verb (do, does, did, have, can, etc.) before the subject, just like in a question. This is used for emphasis when we start a sentence with negative words like 'Never', 'Seldom', or 'Hardly'.

rule_cards.name: The Negative Start
rule_cards.correct: Never have I seen such a beautiful view.
rule_cards.incorrect: Never I have seen such a beautiful view.

rule_cards.name: Not Only... But Also
rule_cards.formula: Not only + Aux + Subject + Verb..., but also...
rule_cards.correct: Not only did he arrive late, but he also forgot his notes.
rule_cards.incorrect: Not only he arrived late, but also...

rule_cards.name: Seldom & Hardly
rule_cards.correct: Seldom does she complain about her work.
rule_cards.incorrect: Seldom she complains about her work.

rule_cards.name: The 'Only' Rule
rule_cards.correct: Only when the rain stopped did we go outside.
rule_cards.incorrect: Only when the rain stopped we went outside.

head_noun_tasks.explanation: 'Never' is the negative adverbial that triggers the inversion of 'have I'.
'Not only' at the start forces 'was' to move before 'it'.
'Only after' requires inversion in the main clause ('did he realize').
'Hardly' triggers the past perfect inversion 'had the movie started'.

drill_tasks.question: Never ________ such a rude person in my life.
drill_tasks.explanation: Starting with 'Never' requires auxiliary before subject.

drill_tasks.question: Not only ________ the prize, but he also set a new record.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'Not only' requires inversion. Since it's past tense ('set'), use 'did'.

drill_tasks.question: Only after he finished his work ________ to bed.
drill_tasks.explanation: The second part of an 'Only after' structure must be inverted.

drill_tasks.question: Hardly ________ the station when the train left.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'Hardly... when' typically uses past perfect inversion.

boss_fight.paragraph: Never I have felt so tired. Not only the project was difficult, but it was also long. Seldom we get a chance to rest like this.

errors.explanation: 'Not only' at the start requires the verb 'was' before the subject.
'Seldom' requires the auxiliary verb 'do' before the subject.

success_feedback: Excellent! You've mastered the basic inversion triggers. Your writing is becoming much more sophisticated.
suggested_next_steps: Learn about 'Little' and 'Rarely' as inversion triggers.
Practice using inversion with conditional sentences (e.g., 'Had I known').
Try Level 5 for more complex negative adverbials!
